generateObject.signature: generateObject<SCHEMA extends FlexibleSchema<unknown>>({model, schema, schemaName?, schemaDescription?, system?, prompt?, messages?, output?: 'object'|'array'|'enum'|'no-schema', maxRetries?, abortSignal?, timeout?, experimental_repairText?, experimental_telemetry?, ...}) → Promise<GenerateObjectResult<Object>>
generateObject.result_shape: { object: OBJECT, reasoning: string|undefined, finishReason, usage, warnings, request, response, ... }
generateObject.throws: NoObjectGeneratedError when the SDK cannot produce or validate an object matching the supplied schema
generateObject.guarantee_clarification: generateObject VALIDATES model output against the supplied schema at the SDK boundary — for providers with native structured-output support, the SDK requests structured output; for providers without, the SDK requests JSON and validates. Either way, invalid or missing structured output surfaces as a typed failure (NoObjectGeneratedError / NoOutputGeneratedError), NOT as a raw text that must be parsed by application code. We do NOT claim: (a) that the provider itself guarantees native JSON-schema enforcement in every execution mode, or (b) that invalid structured output can never occur. What we DO claim: the application no longer performs manual JSON.parse on unrestricted free-form provider text; residual structured-output failure remains possible but is now surfaced as a typed error and handled via our sanitized error taxonomy — never as a JSON.parse crash echoed to the client.

Output (via `output as Output`).purpose: used with generateText's `output` or `experimental_output` parameter to request structured output alongside tool calling
Output (via `output as Output`).signature_hint: Output.object({schema}) returns an Output descriptor consumed by generateText
Output (via `output as Output`).note: less direct than generateObject for a route with no tool calls; generateObject is the cleaner choice

NoObjectGeneratedError.purpose: error class thrown by generateObject when object generation fails

NoOutputGeneratedError.purpose: thrown when no LLM output at all is produced (empty response, provider silence)

RetryError.purpose: thrown when transport-level retries exhaust their budget

zodSchema.purpose: helper re-exported from @ai-sdk/provider-utils; converts a Zod schema into the FlexibleSchema shape generateObject expects

jsonSchema.purpose: helper for using raw JSON Schema (JSON Schema draft) as a FlexibleSchema — alternative to Zod
jsonSchema.advantage: avoids introducing a direct Zod dependency if we want zero-new-dep hardening

retry_semantics.meaning: transport-level retry on provider errors (429, 5xx, timeouts) — retries the SAME request. Does NOT re-generate on model output that fails schema validation.
retry_semantics.on_malformed_output: generateObject throws NoObjectGeneratedError immediately; no implicit re-invocation of the model
retry_semantics.recommended_setting_for_our_route: maxRetries: 0 — to honor the 'one provider call per classify request' policy strictly and eliminate any transport-level retry ambiguity

repair_semantics.experimental_repairText: optional callback (RepairTextFunction). If set, invoked with the raw text on parse failure to attempt repair BEFORE throwing NoObjectGeneratedError. WE WILL NOT SET IT — violates 'no silent semantic repair' and 'no additional model call for repair' policies.

classification_schema.policy: VALIDATION ONLY — no transforms of any kind. No trim, no lowercase, no dedup, no defaults, no enum normalization, no coercion, no repair, no semantic rewriting, no silent removal of duplicate entries, no silent stripping of unknown keys. All non-conforming output must fail schema validation and be surfaced as a typed failure via the route's error taxonomy.

archetype.on_invalid: schema validation fails → hardening returns sanitized 502 with error category structured_output_invalid (raw output NOT echoed to client)

company_preferences.duplicate_policy: REJECT via deterministic refinement — exact-duplicate entries within the array fail schema validation. Case-different values (e.g. 'anthropic' vs 'Anthropic') REMAIN DISTINCT and pass; the product contract does not currently forbid case-different variants.
company_preferences.note: Prior draft proposed silent trim + case-insensitive dedup; corrected here per reviewer feedback: validation only, no silent transforms.

reasoning.whitespace_only_policy: REJECT via deterministic refinement — a string consisting only of whitespace fails schema validation. It is NOT silently rewritten or trimmed.

classification_schema.unknown_key_policy: STRICT REJECTION — reject unknown top-level keys via schema failure. Prevents silent contamination if the model invents fields. Unknown keys are NOT silently dropped.
classification_schema.coercion_policy: NONE — wrong-type field fails schema validation.
classification_schema.defaulting_policy: NONE — no silent defaults. Missing required field fails schema validation.
classification_schema.transform_policy: NONE — the schema performs validation only. No trim, no lowercase, no dedup, no normalization, no repair.
classification_schema.object_mode: STRICT — `z.object({...}).strict()` (Zod) or `additionalProperties: false` (JSON Schema fallback). Unknown keys cause validation failure.

options.malformed_json_prevention: STRONG — SDK enforces schema; malformed → NoObjectGeneratedError not free-form parse
options.semantic_validation: STRONG — enum values, string bounds, unknown-key rejection enforced at SDK boundary

options.implementation_complexity: LOW — replace generateText + JSON.parse with generateObject; delete the parse try/catch and stripping logic
options.sdk_compatibility: supported in ai@6.0.182 (confirmed via node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts inspection)
options.deterministic_behavior: STRONG — success returns typed .object; failure throws NoObjectGeneratedError with structured metadata
options.privacy_impact: NEUTRAL — we control error path and can sanitize before responding to client
options.caller_compatibility: PRESERVED — success shape unchanged; failure response can drop raw/detail without breaking caller (verified)
options.testability: HIGH — helper can be extracted into a pure module and unit-tested with mocked model
options.residual_failure_modes: provider outage (500) · rate limit (500) · schema validation still can fail if provider returns valid JSON with wrong-shape → NoObjectGeneratedError handled as sanitized 502

options.name: generateText + strict runtime schema validation + no repair

options.name: generateText + bounded local JSON extraction/repair

options.residual_failure_modes: silent semantic drift (repair changes meaning); repair opens attack surface for prompt injection
options.recommendation: REJECT — violates 'no silent semantic repair' policy

options.name: Prompt-only hardening (stricter instructions)

selected_option.primary_rationale: generateObject is fully supported by ai@6.0.182; it validates model output against the supplied schema at the SDK boundary; eliminates the current manual JSON.parse of unrestricted free-form provider text; produces typed .object on success; surfaces schema/generation failure as a typed error (NoObjectGeneratedError); zero silent repair; one provider call with explicit maxRetries:0 policy; caller-compatible success contract (field + type compatible, not byte-identical); safe to strip raw/detail from client 502 (verified against caller and harness dependencies).
selected_option.fallback: B (generateText + explicit runtime schema validation, no repair, no retry) — reserved for the specific case where a demonstrated generateObject × @ai-sdk/anthropic incompatibility is discovered before the code change lands. Not a preference; only a compatibility escape hatch.
selected_option.schema_input_choice: Zod, imported directly as `import { z } from "zod"`. Passed to generateObject as `schema: <ZodSchema>`.

risks: Small chance that a specific interaction between generateObject and @ai-sdk/anthropic's Sonnet 4.6 provider path is unsupported for a particular schema shape (e.g. deeply nested arrays). Mitigation: the classify schema is shallow (4 top-level fields, 3 primitives + 1 flat string array); this is well within any known constraint.

generateObject enforces schema at the SDK boundary but the Anthropic model must still emit output that the SDK can constrain. For providers without native structured-output support, the SDK falls back to prompt-based JSON extraction. Anthropic has native support for JSON via tool use / response_format; the ai SDK's Anthropic provider uses this. Verified indirectly via node_modules; explicit verification is worth doing during implementation-loop inspection.
Adding zod as a direct dep is a trivial diff but requires explicit approval; skipping the direct-dep addition and using jsonSchema() means slightly less ergonomic TypeScript for the schema author.

Removing `raw` from the 502 body loses one debugging lever. Mitigation: retain bounded server-side ~500-char excerpt at ERROR level with correlation_id; harness continues to capture body_excerpt which will now be sanitized text.

The current classify system prompt was written assuming free-form JSON output. Under generateObject the prompt should remain semantically identical (define archetypes + user intent) but may benefit from removing the 'Return ONE JSON object' instruction because the SDK enforces JSON. If prompt is changed at all in the implementation loop, the design must justify it.

Setting maxRetries:0 removes transport-level retry, so a transient Anthropic 429 or 5xx during classify would immediately propagate as 429/502/504 in our error taxonomy. This is aligned with the 'one call per request' policy and is preferable to hidden retries.

Adding correlation_id changes the failure body shape; while the caller reads only err.error, external monitoring or log-scrape tools (none currently exist for this app) might parse other fields. Low risk.

The reasoning field's 2000-char upper bound is a guess; if the Anthropic model tends to write longer reasoning under structured output, the implementation loop may need to raise the bound. Mitigation: pick a bound that comfortably fits observed A-run reasoning + margin.

The company_preferences 10-item upper bound is a guess; if fixtures ever legitimately name >10 companies, we would reject valid output. Mitigation: sample observed A-run outputs during implementation.

Tests are mocked; no real API interaction means we can't catch a specific provider-side regression. Acceptable for the hardening design because the SEPARATE cost-approved Fixture B rerun (after implementation) provides the end-to-end validation.
